logic: Count distinct outgoing payee accounts for every evaluation account, returning 0 for accounts without outgoing transfers.
business_explanation: Outgoing recipient count measures payment-network breadth and supports interpretable review of counterparty dispersion.
sql: SELECT account.unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT transfer.dst) AS value FROM evaluation_accounts AS account LEFT JOIN edges AS transfer ON transfer.src = account.unique_id AND transfer.relation = 'personal_wechat_pay_transfer_payer_side' GROUP BY account.unique_id

logic: Follow the account-to-natural-person binding and then the natural-person-to-customer binding, counting distinct linked individual customers for every evaluation account.
business_explanation: The two-hop count describes customer records reachable through a natural-person identity bridge. Shared identity links can connect accounts but do not alone establish coordinated control.
sql: SELECT account.unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT customer.dst) AS value FROM evaluation_accounts AS account LEFT JOIN edges AS person ON person.src = account.unique_id AND person.relation = 'wechat_pay_account_bind_natural_person' LEFT JOIN edges AS customer ON customer.src = person.dst AND customer.relation = 'natural_person_bind_individual_customer' GROUP BY account.unique_id

logic: Sum outgoing transfer amounts for every evaluation account and convert the stored RMB-fen values to yuan; return 0 when no outgoing edge exists.
business_explanation: Outgoing payment amount summarizes observed monetary scale and complements recipient count by separating payment breadth from transfer value.
sql: SELECT account.unique_id, COALESCE(SUM(transfer.total_amount / 100.0), 0.0) AS value FROM evaluation_accounts AS account LEFT JOIN edges AS transfer ON transfer.src = account.unique_id AND transfer.relation = 'personal_wechat_pay_transfer_payer_side' GROUP BY account.unique_id
